rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People in the Prophetic era sometimes estimated elapsed time by how many verses a reader could recite; a report places the dawn interval after the Prophet’s pre-dawn meal at fifty verses.
rows.anchor: كان بينه وبين طلوع الفجر مقدار ما يقرأ القارئ خمسين آية

rows.speaker: أبو بكر ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says fixing verse boundaries is difficult because verses vary in length and may stop before or after a complete meaning.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر ابن العربي وتحديد الآية من معضلات القرآن ، فمن آياته طويل وقصير

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari holds that verse boundaries are fixed by transmitted authority.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري الآيات علم توقيفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur proposes that a verse’s extent may follow the end of its revelation, with the occurrence of a rhyme-like ending as its sign.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون تعيين مقدار الآية تبعا لانتهاء نزولها وأمارته وقوع الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawasil are recurring words whose final letters or sounds and spoken forms match or nearly match, making their pattern seem deliberate across many verses.
rows.anchor: والذي استخلصته أن الفواصل هي الكلمات التي تتماثل في أواخر حروفها أو تتقارب ، مع تماثل أو تقارب صيغ النطق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawasil are judged by similarity in vocalized and unvocalized word forms; they resemble sajʿ and the poetic device of maintaining a pattern beyond what rhyme requires.
rows.anchor: العبرة فيها بتماثل صيغ الكلمات من حركات وسكون وهي أكثر شبها بالتزام ما لا يلزم في القوافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every such closing is an ayah ending even when the sentence’s intended point is unfinished there.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الفواصل كلها منتهى آيات ولو كان الكلام الذي تقع فيه لم يتم فيه الغرض المسوق إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a purpose ends without a fasila, that point is rarely an ayah ending; the opening of Sad is an exception counted as an ayah without a fasila.
rows.anchor: إذا انتهى الغرض المقصود من الكلام ولم تقع عند انتهائه فاصلة لا يكون منتهى الكلام نهاية آية إلا نادرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some opening-sura endings use an open consonant followed by long alif, while others use an extended final wāw or yā; Ibn Ashur illustrates both patterns.
rows.anchor: فواصل بنيت على حرف مضموم مشبع بواو . أو على حرف مكسور مشبع بياء ساكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A long passage can remain one ayah when its thought continues to its eventual ending; the passage about David’s judgment is his example.
rows.anchor: فهذه الجمل كلها عدت آية واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawasil contribute to the Qur’an’s inimitability as verbal embellishment and eloquence.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الفواصل من جملة المقصود من الإعجاز لأنها ترجع إلى محسنات الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing at each fasila lets its sound affect listeners and makes them feel the beauty of the patterned wording, as in poetry and sajʿ.
rows.anchor: فمن الغرض البلاغي الوقوف عند الفواصل لتقع في الأسماع فتتأثر نفوس السامعين بمحاسن ذلك التماثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ayah boundary may divide syntactically connected wording: the cited verses in Ghafir and Hud continue into the next ayah, yet should still be paused at.
rows.anchor: وينبغي الوقف عند نهاية كل آية منها . وقوله تعالى ) واشهدوا أني بريء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignoring poetic rhyme endings spoils the poet’s craft and turns poetry into prose; ignoring sajʿ endings likewise wastes a deliberate verbal refinement.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن من الإضاعة لدقائق الشعر أن يلقيه ملقيه على مسامع الناس دون وقف عند قوافيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The desire to explain meaning does not excuse a reciter from preserving these endings: explaining is a lecturer’s task, not a poem reciter’s task.
rows.anchor: فإن البيان وظيفة ملقي درس لا وظيفة منشد الشعر ، ولو كان هو الشاعر نفسه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Al-Itqan transmits from Abu Amr that some authorities say pausing at the verse endings is Sunnah.
rows.anchor: وفي الإتقان عن أبي عمرو قال بعضهم : الوقف على رؤوس الآي سنة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi’s report in Shuʿab al-Iman calls pausing at verse endings preferable even when their syntax connects forward, following the Prophet’s practice.
rows.anchor: عن البيهقي في شعب الإيمان : الفضل الوقف على رؤوس الآيات وان تعلقت بما بعدها

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Umm Salama that the Prophet recited in verse-by-verse units, pausing after each ayah.
rows.anchor: عن أم سلمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ قطع قراءته آية آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported verse boundaries must be followed, as Ibn al-Arabi and al-Zamakhshari stress, though their transmission does not prevent seeking useful general indicators.
rows.anchor: وجوب اتباع المأثور من تحديد الآي كما قال ابن العربي والزمخشري ولكن ذلك لا يصدنا عن محاولة ضوابط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some opening disjoint-letter groups count as verses and others do not, so the proposed indicators admit exceptions.
rows.anchor: ولم تعد ألر . ألمر . طس~ . ص~ . ق~ . ن~ . آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of verses was fixed by the Prophet under revelation brought by Gabriel, who recited each newly revealed verse in its designated place.
rows.anchor: فكانت وحيا نزل به جبريل ، فقرئ مع الآية التي نزل بأثرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosquito parable in al-Baqara follows the promise of the Garden because it answers polytheists who objected that Muhammad should not give examples of a fly or spider, then moves from one parable to their objection.
rows.anchor: كان ردا على المشركين في قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse placement may have an apparent connection, but sometimes its occasion explains its position even when the surrounding topic seems unrelated, as with the passage about revelation in al-Qiyama.
rows.anchor: وقد لا تكون له مناسبة ولكنه اقتضاه سبب في ذلك المكان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports Ibn Abbas saying that when Gabriel brought revelation, the Prophet moved his tongue and lips to memorize it, prompting the passage in al-Qiyama.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله إذا نزل جبريل بالوحي كان مما يحرك به لسانه وشفتيه يريد أن يحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verse may follow the last verse revealed during the sura’s revelation period because its occasion occurred then, even if the thematic link is not apparent.
rows.anchor: قد يكون سبب وضعها في موضعها أنها قد نزلت على سبب وكان حدوث سبب نزولها في مدة نزول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to guard the prayers was placed amid many rules about spouses and mothers, and Ibn Ashur says he discussed its occasion at that verse.
rows.anchor: بين تشريعات أحكام كثيرة في شؤون الأزواج والأمهات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur cites Ibn Abbas’s report that the command to fear the Day of Return was appended after the sura’s completion by an instruction to place it after a specified verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في آية ) واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله (

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In Sahih Muslim, Ibn Masud reports that the opening of al-Hadid was revealed in Mecca, while its passage beginning with the call to spend was revealed in Medina.
rows.anchor: ما روى في صحيح مسلم عن ابن مسعود أن أول سورة الحديد نزل بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The late Medinan passage in al-Hadid fits the sura through thematic relation and similarity of style; its delayed revelation was likely tied to a later occasion.
rows.anchor: فلا يكون ذلك إلا لمناسبة بينها وبين آي تلك السورة والتشابه في أسلوب النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because reports fixing verse placement are few, an exegete should seek a plausible relation wherever possible and otherwise avoid forced explanations.
rows.anchor: كان حقا على المفسر أن يتطلب مناسبات لمواقع الآيات ما وجد إلى ذلك سبيلا موصلا وإلا فليعرض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s main purpose is reforming the whole community: calling unbelievers to faith and sound worship, and guiding believers’ morals, steadfastness, success, and purification.
rows.anchor: إن الغرض الأكبر للقرآن هو إصلاح الأمة بأسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because each verse serves reform, proof, guidance, or correction, the Qur’an need not proceed as a continuous treatise; like a preacher, it shifts among current concerns and inserts instructive parenthetical statements.
rows.anchor: لأن كل آية منه ترجع إلى غرض الإصلاح والاستدلال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited passage about a faction of the People of the Book, the sentence declaring that guidance is God’s guidance is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: إن الهدى هدى الله ( جملة معترضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about occasions of revelation can explain a general, obscure, or concise expression, themselves supply the interpretation, or prompt the exegete to seek further evidence.
rows.anchor: إن من أسباب النزول ما ليس المفسر بغنى عن علمه لأن فيها بيان مجمل أو إيضاح خفي وموجز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas explains to Marwan that the verse concerns Jews who concealed the answer to the Prophet’s question, then sought praise for a false answer and rejoiced in concealing the truth.
rows.anchor: فأجاب ابن عباس قائلا : إنما دعا النبي اليهود فسألهم على شيء فكتموه إياه وأخبروه بغيره

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In al-Muwatta, Aisha corrects ʿUrwa: the verse was revealed about Ansar who had worshipped Manat and felt scruple about saʿy until they asked the Prophet after Islam.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة : كلا ، لو كان كما تقول لكانت فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some occasions of revelation help recover rhetorical features by reconstructing the context and communicative situation of a verse.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما ينبه المفسر إلى إدراك خصوصيات بلاغية تتبع مقتضى المقامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reviewing reports with sound chains, Ibn Ashur classifies occasions of revelation into five kinds.
rows.anchor: وقد تصفحت أسباب النزول التي صحت أسانيدها فوجدتها خمسة أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first kind is an occasion whose knowledge is necessary to understand the intended meaning; it includes explanations of Qur’anic ambiguities.
rows.anchor: الأول : هو المقصود من الآية يتوقف فهم المراد منها على علمه فلابد من البحث عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second kind consists of events that prompt legislation but do not clarify ambiguity or alter a verse’s general, specific, or conditional scope; they illustrate its ruling.
rows.anchor: والثاني : هو حوادث تسببت عليها تشريعات أحكام وصور تلك الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the second kind, scholars agree or nearly agree that the occasion does not restrict the rule to that incident; legislation is presumed general.
rows.anchor: إذ قد اتفق العلماء أو كادوا على أن سبب النزول في مثل هذا لا يخصص ، واتفقوا على أن أصل التشريع

rows.speaker: عويمر العجلاني
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur gives the report about ʿUwaymir al-ʿAjlani as an example of an event that occasioned the legislation of liʿan.
rows.anchor: مثل حديث عويمر العجلاني الذي نزلت عنه آية اللعان

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: The report about Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra occasioned the rule for a sick person or someone with a scalp ailment, and Kaʿb said its rule was general despite his particular case.
rows.anchor: فقد قال كعب بن عجرة : هي لي خاصة ولكم عامة

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama asked why men fight while women do not; Ibn Ashur cites the verse against coveting others’ advantages as the resulting revelation.
rows.anchor: ومثل قول أم سلمة رضي الله عنها للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : يغزو الرجال ولا نغزو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab proverbs originally evoked eloquent descriptions of symbolic situations; as usage continued, people forgot the situation and retained the proverb’s point, while the Qur’an develops its parables explicitly and inventively.
rows.anchor: لما تداولتها الألسن في الاستعمال وطال عليها الأمد نسيت الأحوال التي وردت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s constructed parables include disbelievers’ deeds as storm-driven ash, the associator falling from heaven, a mirage, and the futile water-seeker in this verse.
rows.anchor: فقد أوضح الأمثال وأبدع تركيبها كقوله تعالى ) مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uses varied styles; suras have distinctive tones, and some are built on recurring fawasil while others are not.
rows.anchor: فإن بعضها بني على فواصل وبعضها ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some suras open ceremonially with praise, an address to believers, or alif-lam-mim and a declaration of the Book, like introductions in literary composition.
rows.anchor: منها ما افتتح بالاحتفال كالحمد ، ويا أيها الذين آمنوا ، وآلم ذلك الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other suras begin by attacking their subject immediately, as in the opening of Muhammad and the declaration at the start of al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما افتتح بالهجوم على الغرض من أول الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s concision can let most verses yield several meanings consistent with their wording; compatible possibilities may coexist, while even exclusive possibilities can prompt the reminder’s intended response.
rows.anchor: صلوحية معظم آياته لأن تؤخذ منها معان متعددة كلها تصلح لها العبارة باحتمالات لا ينافيها اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s layered meanings would take many times its length to express without this concision, and its subtle signs may exceed a scholar’s notice.
rows.anchor: ولولا إيجاز القرآن لكان أداء ما يتضمنه من المعاني في أضعاف مقدار القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic ellipsis always has a clue in the wording or context, while also allowing much meaning in few words.
rows.anchor: ولكنك لا تعثر على حذف يخلو الكلام من دليل عليه من لفظ أو سياق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls deletion and abbreviation a characteristic method of revelation; Ibn Ashur cites a Roman bishop’s remark that a verse gathers what was revealed to Jesus about this life and the next.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف في سورة المدثر الحذف والاختصار هو نهج التنزيل

rows.speaker: أحد بطارقة الروم
rows.claim: A Roman bishop told Umar that the verse about obeying God and His Messenger gathers what was revealed to Jesus concerning worldly and afterlife matters.
rows.anchor: قال بعض بطارقة الروم لعمر بن الخطاب لما سمع قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation to Moses’ mother compresses two commands, two prohibitions, and two glad tidings into one passage.
rows.anchor: جمع بين أمرين ونهيين وبشارتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic phrase about life through retaliation is more concise than the familiar Arab saying that killing most effectively prevents killing.
rows.anchor: مقابلا أوجز كلام عرف عندهم وهو القتل أنفى للقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki extensively analyzes the eloquence of the earth-and-heaven command, while al-Baqillani treats distinctive features of al-Naml.
rows.anchor: بسط السكاكي في المفتاح آخر قسم البيان نموذجا مما اشتملت عليه هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the exchange about Saqar, Ibn Ashur supplies omitted speech: those discussing the criminals ask the informed among them, who say they asked the criminals what put them in Saqar.
rows.anchor: أي يتذاكرون شأن المجرمين فيقول من علموا شأنهم سألناهم هم فقلنا ما سلككم في سقر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the question is not an explanation of the discussion: it quotes the questioners and the criminals’ answer that they did not pray.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف قوله ) ما سلككم في سقر ( ليس ببيان للتساؤل عنهم وإنما هو حكاية قول المسؤولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another concise construction omits a governing noun, as in the declaration that righteousness is whoever believes in God.
rows.anchor: ومنه حذف المضاف كثيرا كقوله تعالى ) ولكن البر من آمن بالله (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted clause can be supplied from context: after God tells Moses to strike the sea, the text leaves implicit that Moses struck it before it parted.
rows.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى ) وأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر فانفلق (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A text may state a general rule while intending a particular case, yielding the general rule, the specific ruling, and the benefit of identifying that case as part of the general class.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك الإخبار عن أمر خاص بخبر يعمه وغيره لتحصل فوائد : فائدة الحكم العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an names the revealed speech collected in the 114 suras from al-Fatiha to al-Nas; it became a proper name for this revelation.
rows.anchor: أولاها الفاتحة وأخراها سورة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name may be a verbal noun on the faʿlan pattern or a proper name; Ibn Ashur derives it from reading because the first revelation began with “Read in your Lord’s name.”
rows.anchor: لأنه مشتق من القراءة لأن أول ما بدئ به الرسول من الوحي ) اقرأ باسم ربك (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce Qur’an with hamza throughout the revelation; Ibn Kathir alone reads it with a lengthened alif after the ra, following a Hijazi dialect that lightens hamza.
rows.anchor: ولذلك اتفق أكثر القراء على قراءة لفظ قرآن مهموزا حيثما وقع في التنزيل ولم يخالفهم إلا ابن كثير قرأه بفتح الراء بعدها ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says variant readings generally agree in the meaning of the word despite differing in its form.
rows.anchor: والأصل توافق القراءات في مدلول اللفظ المختلف في قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported alternative derives Qur’an from qarn, joining, because its suras, verses, and letters are joined; on that view it is not from qara’a, and Ibn Kathir’s form fits as another name for the Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو قرآن بوزن فعال ، من القرن بين الأشياء أي الجمع بينها لأنه قرنت سوره بعضها ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some derive Qur’an from qarina, signifying mutually confirming verses, but Ibn Ashur rejects the proposed collective plural because this form’s known plurals do not include it.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن قرآن جمع قرينه أي اسم جمع ، إذ لا يجمع مثل قرينه على وزن فعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an is the most famous and frequently used name for Muhammad’s revelation; al-Itqan lists more than twenty names or descriptions, with six commonly used names.
rows.anchor: وهو أشهر أسمائه وأكثرها ورودا في آياته وأشهرها دورانا على ألسنة السلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other six common names are al-Tanzil, al-Kitab, al-Furqan, al-Dhikr, al-Wahy, and Kalam Allah.
rows.anchor: والذي اشتهر إطلاقه عليه منها ستة : التنزيل ، والكتاب ، والفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Furqan originally means what distinguishes truth from falsehood; it is a verbal noun used for the Battle of Badr’s day and became a proper name for the Qur’an, like Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: فأما الفرقان فهو في الأصل اسم لما يفرق به بين الحق والباطل وهو مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al Imran first calls the revelation the Book, then calls it al-Furqan after naming Torah and Gospel, signaling that al-Furqan is the proper name of Muhammad’s Book.
rows.anchor: فوصفه أولا بالكتاب وهو اسم الجنس العام ثم عبر عنه باسم الفرقان عقب ذكر التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an merits the name al-Furqan because it distinguishes truth from falsehood through proofs and parables, especially in its teaching of monotheism and God’s attributes.
rows.anchor: ووجه تسميته الفرقان أنه امتاز عن بقية الكتب السماوية بكثرة ما فيه من بيان التفرقة بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an condenses the virtues attributed to Muhammad’s companions in earlier scriptures into the declaration that the community is the best nation.
rows.anchor: فلما وصفهم القرآن قال ) كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its legal rulings are clear and resistant to doubt; the polygyny rule is Ibn Ashur’s example of guidance absent from Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: وأما إن افتقدت ناحية آيات أحكامه فإنك تجدها مبرأة من اللبس وبعيدة عن تطرق الشبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s clarity in law exemplifies its role as guardian over earlier scriptures, a point Ibn Ashur says he will explain at the opening of Al Imran.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى ) وأنزلنا عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tanzil is the verbal noun of “send down,” applied to the revealed text because its wording descended from heaven.
rows.anchor: وأما التنزيل فهو مصدر نزل ، أطلق على المنزل باعتبار أن ألفاظ القرآن أنزلت من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories teach that God’s power exceeds every power and that He supports those who support Him; taking the means of preparedness and reliance protects people from others’ domination.
rows.anchor: من ينصره ، وأنهم إن أخذوا بوسيلتي البقاء : من الاستعداد والاعتماد ؛ سلموا من تسلط غيرهم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah’s rescue from distress illustrates God’s favorable outcome for the righteous and His deliverance of believers.
rows.anchor: فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم ، وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories also yield incidental lessons about the history of law and civilization, encouraging Muslims to attend to the benefits of civil life.
rows.anchor: الفائدة العاشرة : أنها يحصل منها بالتبع فوائد في تاريخ التشريع والحضارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a reading with kasra on the dal, “the king’s dīn” in Joseph means Pharaoh’s law; Ibn Ashur infers Egyptian law permitted enslavement of a thief.
rows.anchor: في قراءة من قرأ دين بكسر الدال ، أي في شرع فرعون يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s refusal to take anyone except the person holding the stolen property indicates that their law did not permit taking a substitute as a slave and that a free person could be owned only on a valid basis.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن شريعتهم ما كانت تسوغ أخذ البدل في الاسترقاق ، وأن الحر لا يملك إلا بوجه معتبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s dispatch of gatherers to the cities suggests that Egypt under Moses had a system of heralds who spread important news.
rows.anchor: أن نظام مصر في زمن موسى إرسال المؤذنين والبريح بالإعلام بالأمور المهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ proposal to put Joseph in a roadside well indicates travelers used short wells along roads to draw water.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا يعلمون وجود الأجباب في الطرقات وهي آبار قصيرة يقصدها المسافرون للاستقاء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s fear that a wolf would eat Joseph shows that predatory wolves then inhabited the Syrian desert toward Egypt, though they have since disappeared there.
rows.anchor: أن بادية الشام إلى مصر كانت توجد بها الذئاب المفترسة وقد انقطعت منها اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that one telling of a story should suffice is answered by the Qur’an’s sermon-like form: stories recur when occasions make them evidence for different aims.
rows.anchor: هو بالخطب والمواعظ أشبه منه بالتآليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preacher who gives related sermons on separate occasions is repeating meanings, not repeating the same speech, because each occasion calls for its own wording and purpose.
rows.anchor: بل إنه أعاد معانيها ولم يعد ألفاظ خطبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One benefit of retelling is that repetition makes the stories more firmly established in people’s minds.
rows.anchor: أحدها رسوخها في الأذهان بتكريرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another benefit is rhetorical: later tellings vary meanings, figures, vocabulary, and constructions, making repetition a demonstration of eloquence and inimitability.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك من الحدود القصوى في البلاغة ، فذلك وجه من وجوه الإعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who missed a story before converting or while absent hear it when it is revealed; hearing it at revelation affects them more than seeking it from someone who memorized it.
rows.anchor: فإن تلقي القرآن عند نزوله أوقع في النفوس من تطلبه من حافظيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since few believers memorize the whole Qur’an, people who know different suras each learn a story through the passage they memorized.
rows.anchor: أن جمع المؤمنين جميع القرآن حفظا كان نادرا بل تجد البعض يحفظ بعض السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tellings vary to avoid excessive length and select different lessons in different places; their combined passages complete the story or its purpose, and some clarify others.
rows.anchor: فيحصل من متفرق مواضعها في القرآن كمال القصة أو كمال المقصود منها
